audit_findings.title: Current debt interest burden is absent from the FY2025 owner-earnings anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: computed $2.195 million annual pre-tax interest and approximately $1.725 million after tax; approximately $0.97 per share of base value
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring after-tax interest reduces equity-level owner earnings because the methodology retains interest expense and does not deduct debt principal in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025 and December 31, 2024, the Company had no outstanding balances under the Credit Agreement.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated timing mismatch: the $48.3 million FY2025 anchor contains almost no interest, while the June 2026 capital structure includes a $44.8 million term loan at 4.9% maturing in 2036. Applying the filed 21.4% interim tax rate produces an approximately $1.725 million annual owner-earnings burden. Scaling the base operating PV to that reduction lowers base value by about $27.1 million, or $0.97 per share, from $28.72 to approximately $27.75. That does not alter the conclusion relative to the $51.45 market price.
audit_findings.action: Rerun all scenarios with the term loan's contractual after-tax interest expense in projected owner earnings, together with any recurring operating savings or costs arising from ownership of the financed properties.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition contingent consideration may be an omitted senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $15.946 million at June 30, 2026, equal to approximately $0.57 per share and 2.0% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquisition consideration requiring future cash settlement is a claim ahead of common equity and should be deducted in the equity bridge when its principal payments are not captured in owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has contingent liabilities related to future internal performance milestones and the estimated value of acquired inventory that may be sold above its net realizable value.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing resolves the balance uncertainty: Level 3 contingent liabilities were $15.946 million, including $6.382 million classified as current. They are distinct from the $44.8 million term loan and absent from the stated bridge, making the omission demonstrated unless another bridge line already captures them. A full $15.946 million deduction would reduce base value from $28.72 to about $28.15 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion relative to the $51.45 price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $6.382 million current amount to the implied long-term component, confirm none is included in debt or another bridge line, and rerun the bridge with the confirmed outstanding contingent consideration deducted.

audit_findings.title: The historical owner-earnings economics may not survive the manufacturing transition
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed six-month 2026 property-and-equipment purchases were $74.820 million, versus the $48.3 million owner-earnings anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Higher recurring maintenance capital, working capital, compliance costs and fixed operating costs would reduce owner earnings and reinvestment returns; successful internal manufacturing and margin gains could increase owner earnings and growth.
audit_findings.evidence: Pursuant to our decision to invest in manufacturing and supply chain assets, our capital requirements and capital allocation decisions will fundamentally change which may introduce additional operational, environmental and other risks.
audit_findings.explanation: The transition is no longer merely prospective. Property and equipment rose from $15.797 million to $104.460 million, the company acquired manufacturing capacity in China, and $12.9 million of construction in progress relates primarily to manufacturing equipment. The filed spending exceeds one full year of anchor owner earnings, but the record does not separate growth investment from steady-state maintenance requirements or quantify expected margin benefits. Either effect is reasonably capable of changing the modeled owner-earnings conversion and growth conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the facility and equipment ramp plan, production-volume assumptions, expected gross-margin savings, incremental working capital, environmental and operating costs, and steady-state maintenance capital; then rebuild owner earnings and RONTA under downside, expected and successful-ramp cases.

audit_findings.title: China minority ownership can create a numerator-denominator mismatch
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed NCI-attributed income was $0.363 million in FY2025 and $0.423 million in the first half of 2026, with NCI equity of $12.431 million at June 30, 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Using 100% of consolidated China cash generation while dividing by only XPEL common shares overstates owner earnings per share unless the minority share is removed from earnings and cash-flow adjustments or NCI is deducted in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: On September 9, 2025, the Company acquired certain assets from its exclusive distributor in China through the formation of a new majority-owned subsidiary, XPEL New Materials Technology Shanghai Limited, in which the Company obtained a 76 % controlling interest.
audit_findings.explanation: The financial statements separately remove NCI from reported net income attributable to XPEL shareholders, but that does not establish that the owner-earnings reconciliation also allocated depreciation, capital expenditures and working-capital movements. The known NCI earnings are small relative to the $48.3 million anchor, but they cover only a partial ownership period and precede the additional 75%-owned China manufacturer. The potential owner-earnings mismatch therefore remains unquantified, and the record cannot establish its materiality.
audit_findings.action: Trace every component of the owner-earnings calculation by legal entity, allocate China earnings and cash-flow adjustments to XPEL's 76% and 75% interests, and rerun; alternatively use consolidated owner earnings and deduct a supportable value for the NCI claims.

audit_findings.title: The cash addition may include unavailable or non-excess foreign cash
audit_findings.magnitude: actual unavailable portion unquantified; maximum exposed bridge amount is the filed $40.675 million, equal to approximately $1.46 per share and 5.1% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Restricted, minority-owned or operationally required cash should be excluded from the cash addition in the equity bridge or reduced for extraction costs and taxes.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company plans to indefinitely reinvest foreign earnings and does not expect to repatriate earnings for the foreseeable future.
audit_findings.explanation: Entity-level availability is unresolved, and the indefinite-reinvestment policy plus PRC distribution restrictions supports examining the bridge. Nevertheless, even the conservative ceiling of removing all $40.675 million would lower base value only from $28.72 to approximately $27.26 per share, still far below the $51.45 market price. The finding therefore cannot change the present valuation conclusion, although the bridge amount should be refined.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 2026 cash balance by entity and jurisdiction, identify minority-owned and restricted balances, estimate required operating liquidity and remittance taxes, and replace the gross cash addition with verified distributable excess cash.

audit_findings.title: A contingent-liability remeasurement benefit may remain in normalized earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: computed $0.613 million pre-tax, approximately $0.493 million after tax and approximately $0.28 per share of base value
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring fair-value gain retained in normalized owner earnings inflates the anchor and all projected operating cash flows and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The valuation adjustments are reflected in general and administrative expenses in the Consolidated Statements of Income for the twelve months ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a $0.613 million downward fair-value adjustment recorded through general and administrative expense, but the supplied record does not establish whether the owner-earnings reconciliation already removed it. If fully retained, applying the filed 19.5% FY2025 tax rate gives an approximately $0.493 million anchor overstatement, about 1.0% of the $48.3 million anchor. Scaling the base operating PV implies roughly a $7.7 million or $0.28-per-share effect, which cannot change the valuation conclusion relative to the $51.45 price.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the FY2025 owner-earnings reconciliation for the $0.613 million adjustment and, if retained, reverse its after-tax effect and rerun all scenarios.
